92507.m: Newborn babies often cry without tears.

92508.q: Roughly how many times a minute does a person blink?
92508.e: A blink only lasts a fraction of a second. We usually blink without noticing.
92508.m: We blink several times a minute without noticing.

92509.q: Why do people wear glasses with specially shaped lenses?
92509.e: Glasses bend the light so that a sharp image forms on the retina. That way you can see clearly again.

92510.q: What is the job called in which you fit and sell glasses?
92510.e: Opticians measure the eyes and make the right lenses. They fit the glasses to the face.
92510.m: You get glasses from an optician.

92511.q: What can you put directly on your eye instead of glasses?
92511.e: Contact lenses are small, thin shells. They sit directly on the cornea and work like the lenses in glasses.
92511.m: Contact lenses sit directly on the eye.

a: You can only see in the dark
92512.e: Short-sighted people see things close up sharply, but things far away look blurred. Glasses can correct this.
92512.m: Short-sighted people see things far away blurred.

92513.e: Long-sighted people find it hard to see things close up sharply. They often see things far away better.
92513.m: Long-sighted people see badly close up.

92514.q: Why do many older people need reading glasses?
a: The lens of the eye gets stiffer
92514.e: With age the lens in the eye can no longer change shape so well. That is why many people over about 45 see blurred close up.
92514.m: Many people need reading glasses as they get older.

92515.q: What happens to glasses in winter when you come into a warm house?
92515.e: The cold lenses cool down the warm, moist air. Tiny water droplets form on the glass.
92515.m: Cold lenses steam up in warm air.

92516.q: What is the part of the glasses that rests on the nose called?
92516.e: The bridge joins the two lenses. It rests on the top of the nose and carries the weight of the glasses.
92516.m: The bridge of the glasses rests on the nose.

92517.q: What does an eye test check?
92517.e: An eye test measures how sharply someone sees. That shows whether glasses are needed.
92517.m: An eye test checks how well your eyes see.

92518.q: What do you often read on the wall during an eye test?
a: Symbols that get smaller and smaller
92518.e: The eye chart has symbols of different sizes. The smaller the symbols you can make out, the better you see.
92518.m: On the eye chart the symbols get smaller and smaller.

92519.q: Why do you cover one eye during an eye test?
a: Because those are the rules of the game
92519.e: Often one eye sees better than the other. That is why each eye is tested on its own.
92519.m: In an eye test each eye is tested separately.

92520.q: What do you have to say in an eye test with rings?
92520.e: In the eye test with Landolt rings, each ring has a small gap. You say whether it is at the top, bottom, left or right.
92520.m: In the ring test you show where the gap is.

92521.q: What are small children shown in an eye test instead of letters?
92521.e: Children who cannot read yet name pictures or show which way symbols point. That way their eyes can be tested too.
92521.m: Small children do the eye test with pictures.

92522.q: For which licence do you need an eye test in Switzerland?
92522.e: Anyone in Switzerland who wants to learn to drive has to take an eye test. Only then do they get a learner driver's permit.
92522.m: You need an eye test to drive a car.

92523.q: What do we call how sharply someone sees?
92523.e: Visual acuity tells you how finely someone can make things out. It is measured in an eye test.
92523.m: An eye test measures visual acuity.

92524.q: Where can you have a simple eye test done?
92524.e: Opticians and eye doctors do eye tests. For detailed examinations you go to an eye doctor.
92524.m: You have an eye test at the optician's or the eye doctor's.

92525.q: What is the doctor who examines and treats eyes called?
92525.e: Eye doctors know all about diseases of the eyes. They can also operate on eyes.
92525.m: For eye problems you go to an eye doctor.

92526.q: Why does the eye doctor sometimes put drops in your eye?
92526.e: With a wide pupil the doctor can see better inside the eye. Afterwards your vision is a little blurry for a few hours.
92526.m: Special drops widen the pupil for the examination.

92527.q: What do you read on a chart on the wall at the eye doctor's?
a: Letters that get smaller and smaller
92527.e: The eye chart has letters or pictures that get smaller and smaller towards the bottom. That shows the doctor how well you see.
92527.m: The eye doctor uses the eye chart to check how well I see.

92528.q: What is a common inflammation called in which the eye turns red and itches?
92528.e: The conjunctiva covers the white of the eye and the inside of the eyelids. When it is inflamed, the eye turns red and itches.
92528.m: With conjunctivitis the eye is red.

92529.q: What is a small, inflamed lump on the eyelid called?
92529.e: A stye is an infection of a small gland at the edge of the eyelid. It is red and sore and usually heals by itself.
92529.m: A stye is an inflammation on the eyelid.

92530.q: What is replaced in an operation for cataracts?
92530.e: With cataracts, the lens in the eye becomes cloudy. In the operation an artificial, clear lens is put in.
92530.m: With cataracts the cloudy lens is replaced.

92531.q: What should you do if something sharp has got into your eye?
a: Don't rub it and go to a doctor
92531.e: Rubbing can injure the eye even more. That is why you go to a doctor or to A&E straight away.
92531.m: With an eye injury, go to a doctor straight away.

92532.q: What does the eye doctor often give you for an eye infection?
a: A plaster cast on your leg
92532.e: Many eye infections are treated with drops or ointment. They are put straight into the eye.
92532.m: Eye infections are often treated with drops.

92533.q: What does having a squint mean?
a: The eyes look in different directions
92533.e: With a squint, the two eyes don't point at the same target. One eye turns inwards, outwards, up or down.
92533.m: With a squint, the eyes don't look in the same direction.

92534.q: What do children with a squint often have stuck over one eye?
92534.e: A special patch covers one eye for a few hours a day. This is a common treatment for a squint.
92534.m: An eye patch helps many children with a squint.

92535.q: Why is the better eye covered when someone has a squint?
a: So the weaker eye gets trained
92535.e: When the good eye is covered, the weaker eye has to work. That way it learns to see better.
92535.m: Covering the good eye trains the weaker eye.

92536.q: Why should a squint in children be treated early?
a: Otherwise one eye learns to see badly
Otherwise the eyes water all the time
92536.e: The brain can ignore the image from the squinting eye. If it is not treated early, this eye stays weak-sighted.
92536.m: A squint is best treated early.

92537.q: What can often help with a squint as well?
92537.e: Some children squint because they are long-sighted. The right glasses can then reduce the squint.
92537.m: Glasses can help with a squint.

92538.q: When is a slight squint still normal in babies?
a: In the first months of life
92538.e: Newborn babies first have to learn to use their eyes together. If the squint lasts longer, an eye doctor should take a look.
92538.m: A brief squint is normal in young babies.

92539.q: What does someone often see if they suddenly start to squint?
92539.e: The two eyes then send two different images. The brain can no longer put them together.
92539.m: A sudden squint can cause double vision.

92540.q: How many muscles move an eye from the outside?
92540.e: Six outer eye muscles pull on each eye. They work together so that both eyes look in the same direction.

92541.q: What is sometimes done for a very strong squint?
a: An operation on the eye muscles
92541.e: In the operation, eye muscles are shortened or moved. Afterwards the eyes are straighter.
92541.m: A strong squint can be operated on.

92542.q: What do good sunglasses protect the eyes from?
92542.e: Good sunglasses keep out the dangerous UV rays. They also soften dazzling light.

92543.q: Where are sunglasses especially important in Switzerland?
a: In the snow in the mountains
92543.e: UV radiation is stronger in the mountains. The snow also reflects a lot of light back into the eyes.
92543.m: You need sunglasses in the snow in the mountains.

92544.q: What can happen in the snow without sunglasses?
92544.e: Too much UV light can burn the cornea. The eyes then hurt badly and you can't see well for a while.
92544.m: Without sunglasses you risk snow blindness.

92545.q: Can you look straight at the sun with sunglasses on?
a: Yes, for as long as you like
92545.e: Even sunglasses don't protect enough against direct sunlight. The eye can be permanently damaged.
92545.m: Never look straight at the sun.

92546.q: What do you need to watch a solar eclipse?
92546.e: Eclipse glasses only let through a tiny part of the light. Ordinary sunglasses are far too bright for this.
92546.m: Only watch a solar eclipse with special glasses.

92547.q: Why are dark glasses without UV protection bad?
a: The pupil gets big and more UV gets in
92547.e: Behind dark lenses the pupil opens. If there is no UV filter, even more harmful radiation then gets into the eye.
92547.m: Sunglasses always need a UV filter.

92548.q: What do people often wear when skiing instead of sunglasses?
92548.e: Ski goggles fit tightly against the face. They protect against sun, wind and snow.
92548.m: People often wear ski goggles when skiing.

92549.q: On which surfaces does the sun reflect especially strongly?
a: On soil and sand in the shade
92549.e: Snow and water reflect a lot of sunlight. The light then also hits the eyes from below.
92549.m: Snow and water reflect sunlight strongly.

92550.q: What helps blind people read texts on a computer?
92550.e: A screen reader reads out the texts on the screen with a computer voice. Some devices also show the text in Braille on a strip you can feel.
92550.m: Screen readers read texts aloud to blind people.

92551.q: Who invented the dot writing system for blind people?
92551.e: He went blind as a small boy. At the age of 15 he developed a writing system made of dots, which is named after him.
92551.m: The dot writing for blind people is named Braille after its inventor.

92552.q: What is the largest number of dots that one Braille character has?
92552.e: A Braille character has six dots in two columns. Depending on which dots are raised, a different letter is formed.
92552.m: A Braille character has up to six dots.

92553.q: Which country did the inventor of the dot writing for blind people come from?
92553.e: The inventor was born in France in 1809. He lived and taught in Paris.
92553.m: The inventor of Braille came from France.

92554.q: What colour is the cane that blind people use?
92554.e: The white cane shows other people that someone is blind. It is used to feel the way ahead.
92554.m: Blind people use a white cane.

92555.q: What helps blind people find their way on the pavement?
92555.e: In Switzerland there are white guide lines with grooves on the ground. You can feel them with a cane or your feet.
92555.m: White guide lines with grooves lead blind people.

92556.q: Which senses help blind people find their way especially well?
92556.e: Blind people pay close attention to sounds and feel their surroundings. That way they make up for part of their missing sight.
92556.m: Blind people find their way using hearing and touch.

92557.q: Where do you often find Braille in everyday life?
92557.e: Many medicine packets have the name in Braille. That way blind people can tell them apart.

92558.q: What is a guide dog for the blind?
a: A dog that leads blind people safely
A dog that searches for avalanche victims
92558.e: A guide dog is specially trained. It leads its person safely around obstacles.
92558.m: A guide dog leads blind people.

92559.q: Which dog breed is often trained as a guide dog?
92559.e: Labradors are calm, friendly and like to learn. That is why they are often trained as guide dogs.

92560.q: What does a guide dog wear when it is working?
92560.e: The guide harness has a firm handle. Through it the person feels every movement of the dog.
92560.m: A guide dog wears a harness.

92561.q: Should you stroke a guide dog while it is working?
a: Yes, but only on the head
92561.e: A working guide dog has to concentrate fully on the way. Distracting it can be dangerous for its person.

92562.q: What does a guide dog do when something is in the way?
a: It leads its person around it
92562.e: A guide dog learns to recognise obstacles. It leads its person safely past them.
92562.m: A guide dog leads around obstacles.

92563.q: Where does a young guide dog live before it is trained?
92563.e: With the puppy-raising family, the young dog gets to know everyday life. After that the real training begins.
92563.m: Young guide dogs grow up with a puppy-raising family.

92564.q: Who decides when to cross the road?
92564.e: The person listens to the traffic and gives the command. The dog then leads them safely across.
92564.m: The person decides when to cross the road.

92565.q: What does a guide dog do in front of stairs?
92565.e: The dog stops in front of stairs and kerbs. That way its person knows a step is coming.
92565.m: A guide dog stops in front of stairs.

92566.q: What do most people who are called colour-blind have?
a: They can only see at night
92566.e: Only very few people are completely colour-blind. Most of them just find it hard to tell certain colours apart.
92566.m: Most colour-blind people only mix up some colours.

92567.q: Which colours are most often mixed up by people with colour vision deficiency?
92567.e: The most common form is red-green colour blindness. People with it see red and green as similar.
92567.m: Red and green are the colours most often mixed up.

92568.q: Who more often has red-green colour blindness?
92568.e: It is inherited in a way that makes it much more common in men. Women are only rarely affected.
92568.m: Men more often have red-green colour blindness.

92569.q: Roughly how many out of 100 men in Europe have red-green colour blindness?
92569.e: In Europe about 8 to 9 out of 100 men are affected. In women it is fewer than 1 in 100.
92569.m: About one man in twelve has red-green colour blindness.

92570.q: How do you test whether someone sees colours well?
a: With pictures made of coloured dots
92570.e: A number made of coloured dots is hidden in the test pictures. People who mix up certain colours cannot see it.
92570.m: A colour test shows numbers made of coloured dots.

92571.q: Where does red-green colour blindness usually come from?
92571.e: Red-green colour blindness is usually inherited. It is not catching and lasts a lifetime.
92571.m: Red-green colour blindness is usually present from birth.

92572.q: What are the sensory cells in the eye that see colours called?
92572.e: The retina has three kinds of these cells for different colours. If one kind is missing, you see colours differently.
92572.m: The cones in the eye see colours.

92573.q: How do colour-blind people know which traffic light is on?
a: By the position of the light
By the sound of the cars
92573.e: The order of the lights on traffic lights is always the same. Red is at the top, green is at the bottom.
92573.m: At traffic lights, the position of the light helps.

92574.q: Why do we see almost no colours at night?
a: The colour cells need a lot of light
92574.e: In the dark, mainly sensory cells that only tell light from dark are working. That is why everything looks grey at night.
92574.m: All cats are grey in the dark, because we can hardly see colours.

92575.q: Why does a banana look yellow?
92575.e: Light contains many colours. The banana skin swallows most of them and mainly reflects yellow back into our eyes.
92575.m: We see the colour that a thing reflects.

92576.q: Which colour reflects almost all light?
92576.e: White things hardly swallow any light. That is why fresh snow is so dazzling in the sun.

92577.q: Which colour swallows almost all light?
92577.e: Black things hardly reflect any light. The swallowed light turns into heat.

92578.q: Why are the leaves of trees green in summer?
a: The green pigment reflects green light
92578.e: Leaves contain a pigment called chlorophyll. It uses red and blue light and reflects the green.
92578.m: Leaves are green because they reflect green light.

92579.q: What is needed for us to see colours?
92579.e: Colours only appear when light falls on things. Without light we can't see any colours.
92579.m: Without light there are no colours to see.

92580.q: Why are light-coloured clothes safer on a bike at night?
a: They reflect more light from headlights
92580.e: Light colours reflect a lot of the light from car headlights. That way the cyclist is seen sooner.
92580.m: Light-coloured clothes are easier to see at night.

92581.q: Why do colourful curtains at a sunny window fade over time?
92581.e: Above all the invisible UV light of the sun breaks down dyes little by little. That is why the colours become pale.

92582.q: What do glow-in-the-dark stars on the bedroom ceiling do when you switch off the light?
a: They keep glowing for a while
92582.e: Glow-in-the-dark paint stores some of the light. In the dark it slowly gives it off again as a faint, often greenish glow.
92582.m: Glow-in-the-dark paint keeps glowing for a while in the dark.

92583.q: Which colour comes right next to red in the rainbow?
92583.e: The colours in the rainbow are always in the same order. Orange comes straight after red.
92583.m: In the rainbow, orange follows red.

92584.q: At what time of day are you most likely to see a rainbow?
92584.e: A rainbow only appears when the sun is low. If the sun is too high, the bow lies below the horizon.
92584.m: Rainbows are usually seen in the morning or evening.

92585.q: What happens if you try to walk to the end of a rainbow?
a: It gets bigger and stays still
92585.e: A rainbow is not a thing in a fixed place. It depends on where you are standing and moves with you.
92585.m: You can never reach a rainbow.

92586.q: What shape would a rainbow have if the ground weren't in the way?
92586.e: From the ground you only see part of the circle. From an aeroplane you can sometimes see the whole circle.
92586.m: A rainbow is really a circle.

92587.q: Can you see a rainbow at night too?
92587.e: With a bright full moon and rain, a moonbow can appear. It is faint and usually looks whitish.
92587.m: Rarely there is a moonbow too.

92588.q: What material is a prism for light experiments usually made of?
92588.e: A prism has to be transparent so that light can pass through it. That is why it is usually made of glass or clear plastic.
92588.m: A prism is made of transparent glass.

92589.q: Which colour is bent the least by a prism?
92589.e: Each colour is bent by a different amount in the glass. Red is bent the least.
92589.m: Red light is bent the least in a prism.

92590.q: What happens if you bring the coloured light from a prism back together?
92590.e: With a lens or a second prism you can combine the colours again. Then white light appears again.
92590.m: All the colours together make white light again.

92591.q: What happens to red laser light in a prism?
a: It stays red and is only bent
92591.e: Red laser light has only one colour. The prism can bend it, but it can't split it into more colours.
92591.m: Light of one colour stays one colour in a prism.

92592.q: What happens to the direction of a beam of light in a prism?
a: It turns round in a circle
92592.e: Light is bent when it goes into the glass and out again at an angle. This bending is called refraction.

92593.q: What at a window can throw colourful spots of light onto the wall?
92593.e: A cut crystal has many slanted faces. It works like a prism and splits the sunlight.
92593.m: Glass crystals at the window make colourful spots of light.

92594.q: Which gemstone sparkles in many colours because it splits light like a prism?
92594.e: A cut diamond bends light very strongly. That is why colourful flashes appear in it.
92594.m: Diamonds sparkle in colours because they split light.
